outcome_branch: Performance-leadership section 6 steps 6-7: wall-clock improvement is present, but tracked guardrail point regressions exceed 2%; production code and the candidate bootstrap tests were reverted. Remaining acceptance criteria do not apply to the rejected outcome.
hypothesis: Sequential BrokerConn::connect_tls_any waits for an unreachable first bootstrap address to exhaust its TCP connect timeout before trying a reachable second address. A fixed four-future first-success race was expected to overlap those attempts and improve ms to first ack while preserving deadlines, negotiation, SASL, retry and cancellation behavior.
finding: The actual pending-TCP fixture makes the approximately 200 ms sequential delay visible. The candidate reduced stalled-first construction-to-first-ack latency by 66.6196% at the median paired point (95% CI -67.5603% to -66.2511%). The refused-first 1-partition and 64-partition paired latency points and the whole-phase allocation-count point exceeded the 2% guardrail limit. Rejection follows the declared acceptance rule; the noisy allocator census is not proof of a causal allocation regression.

experiment.order: AB on even pair indices, BA on odd indices; one fresh process per arm per pair; each process repetition_index=0.
experiment.extension_reason: One extension from five to ten pairs was authorized to resolve the large allocation-census uncertainty. Original five-pair data and analysis remain saved; no samples were removed, no variant was altered, and no further sampling followed the ten-pair rejection.
experiment.case_matrix: live-first, refused-first, and verified stalled-TCP-first; each with 1/6/64 partitions, one acknowledged record per case.
experiment.fixture: Safe loopback TcpSocket.listen(1), two held unaccepted connections, third Tokio TcpStream::connect verified pending until a 50 ms timeout. Fixture setup/proof precedes the measured allocator census; all three fixtures are held in both arms through the entire case matrix. No firewall/routing changes.

same_broker_for_both_arms.binary: nb-serve from the baseline release target; explicitly set through NB_SERVE in all commands.

experiment.production_difference: Only src/net.rs differs in production source between baseline and candidate; candidate.patch also includes the six new bootstrap regression tests. Harness and fixture bytes are identical.

statistics.method: For each process, primary = median of the three stalled-first partition cases; each healthy/partition case also has its own paired series. Paired point = median of 100*(B_i/A_i-1). Percentile 95% CIs bootstrap ten matched pair indices together, 20,000 resamples, seed71002. The separate ratio of arm medians and its pair-resampled CI are retained in ab-analysis.json. Positive deltas mean regression for these cost/latency metrics.

hypothesis_first_reproduction.result: Stalled-first cases approximately 299-304 ms versus approximately 98-100 ms live/refused, with each fixture verifying an actual approximately 51 ms pending TCP connect.

allocations.interpretation: Whole measured-phase allocator census includes runtime activity. The wide paired interval excludes a deterministic causal attribution; its point still exceeds the tracked guardrail limit.

named_open_sockets.unit: socket FDs after first ack per case

guardrails.rule: Reject when any tracked guardrail point regression exceeds 2%; confidence intervals do not waive this rule. Ratio-of-medians observations are retained separately from median paired deltas.

socket_cleanup_and_bounds.measurement_scope: Socket FD count after first ack; not a peak concurrency sampler. Three fixture listeners plus their six prefilled connections remain alive in both arms, along with the case connection/runtime sockets. These constants are included consistently.
socket_cleanup_and_bounds.tests: Four stalled bootstrap attempts delay the fifth reachable address until a slot finishes; two pending SYN_SENT connections disappear after cancellation; accepted TLS losers consume ClientHello and observe EOF/reset after cancellation. Full connection futures, including TCP/TLS phases, are dropped.
socket_cleanup_and_bounds.dns_caveat: Tokio hostname resolution may spawn blocking resolver jobs that outlive cancellation; the cap bounds dial futures/sockets/handshakes, not outstanding resolver-worker jobs.
socket_cleanup_and_bounds.shipped_state: Candidate reverted; production bootstrap dialing remains sequential.

limits: Local unsigned validating-null-broker engineering evidence; not a Kafka comparison or public performance claim. Suite HOLD remains active.

Managed shared host without frequency pinning; CPU3 affinity keeps coordinator builds off that CPU; shared CPU quota, memory/cache and host-wide effects remain possible. CPU/RSS/allocation intervals remain observations with the reported uncertainty.

The real pending-TCP fixture depends on Linux accept-backlog behavior and fails if it cannot verify a pending Tokio connect. It is not a TLS/application delay or a firewall blackhole. The200ms timeout is an explicit fixture configuration, not a production default change.

Candidate cancellation tests cover actual pending TCP and TLS futures. They do not bound outstanding Tokio blocking DNS resolver jobs, which may outlive cancellation. No multi-broker caller overlap, hostname/DNS delay, SASL setup speed, or real-broker network behavior is claimed.
Socket FD observations after first ack are not transient peak FD measurements; candidate cap/loser cleanup are established separately by implementation and behavioral tests.

No deterministic instruction or allocation-improvement route was asserted. Whole-phase allocations include small runtime and sampler activity; wide confidence intervals do not prove a causal allocator regression.
